questions.question: Why does the naive agent forward the attacker's email to all three contacts?
options: It treats an imperative in tool-returned email text as an instruction and calls tool_send for every CONTACTS entry
The trusted user explicitly requested forwarding to Alice, Bob, and Carol
The email tool automatically sends every message it reads
The IFC tag authorizes the email to control the agent
questions.explanation: naive_agent lowercases the retrieved body, finds "forward this", and loops over CONTACTS calling tool_send. The user prompt is not consulted as a trusted authorization for that side effect.

questions.question: Which delivery vector is not indirect prompt injection in the lesson's taxonomy?
options: A poisoned document returned by retrieval
An attacker directly editing the system prompt configuration
An email body read by an inbox workflow
A tool response containing attacker-authored instructions
questions.explanation: IPI enters through external content the agent consumes during normal operation: RAG, inbox/document workflows, or tool output. Directly changing the system prompt is a configuration compromise, not an indirect content injection.

questions.question: Why does the adaptive polite wording bypass the repository's keyword_filter?
options: The filter is disabled after the first static attack
The attacker changes the email sender to a trusted address
It removes markers such as [SYSTEM:] and "forward this" while preserving the imperative intent as "distribute this note"
The filter sees only the user's prompt, not the email body
questions.explanation: The adaptive body says "Kindly distribute this note...". filter_keyword checks a fixed marker list and misses that paraphrase, while the naive imperative detector still acts on "distribute".

questions.question: What invariant does ifc_agent enforce before a tool action?
options: Every retrieved document must be encrypted
The model must run in a single turn
The user must approve every token generated by the model
Untrusted content may be read for summarization but cannot authorize send() without trusted ratification
questions.explanation: ifc_agent tags the email content as untrusted and ignores its control-flow instructions. The trusted user prompt asks only for a summary, so no send call is permitted.

questions.question: What did the adaptive-attack result imply about twelve published IPI defenses in the cited work?
options: Adaptive attacks broke over 90% of the defenses despite near-zero original attack-rate claims
Only static keyword attacks were tested, so every defense was confirmed
The defenses were all immune once the attacker had no gradients
The study evaluated only image-only prompts
questions.explanation: The lesson uses the result to warn that a defense evaluated against a fixed attack distribution can fail under adaptive search. This is the same gap visible between the static and polite bodies in the toy.

questions.question: Where does prompt injection rank in the 2025 OWASP LLM Top 10?
options: LLM05, below supply-chain risks
LLM01, the top application-layer threat
LLM10, the lowest-ranked entry
It is not listed because OWASP covers only infrastructure
questions.explanation: OWASP labels prompt injection LLM01, covering direct and indirect forms. The ranking reinforces that treating retrieved instructions as data is a first-class application-security requirement.
